chapter: Hartford, prison, theater and the Collective
title: Role of cultural institutions and funding
summary: Brower and McLean discuss performance centers presenting artists of stature; McLean thinks enough wealth exists but is hard to raise.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: What do you think the challenge is to American cultural institutions? In my time in working there, there was a lot of – there came to be a point where there was a lot of negative response. I viewed it as crabs in a barrel, of people being jealous. You couldn’t – I mean, if he was artistic director, you would expect him to showcase his people and showcase his sensibility. The real challenge was for other performance centers to decide, let’s make Jimmie Heath artistic director, or let’s make Cecil Taylor artistic – we’ll make some – and then those persons would have the opportunity to bring their galaxy of – their circle to the fore and to present their music and music that they were really interested in. That seems to me to be where – the whole club is unable to frankly support artists of quality and achievement financially. You can’t, with 150 people or 75 people or 80 people, pay a Jackie McLean what he’s worth on a night. You’d have to charge people $80 or $100 a head. So it becomes a prohibitive environment. It seems like these – more performance centers, more cities – and they all have a signature performance center – need to be challenged to do what Lincoln Center does – is doing now, what the Kennedy Center’s doing with Billy Taylor. How do you feel about that?

I think that should be high on the list of things that big cities should be trying to do. That’s why we’re here, doing this. We’re doing it ourselves here. We’re presenting concerts, dance troupes, artists, and different people – painters – coming into this building, into this place, and presenting their work, presenting their music, their productions, here. Also, we’re hoping that in time this will be recognized here in the
north and in the city of Hartford and in the country as being producers of wonderful cultural events, music, dance, what have you.

Do you have a sense that the funding environment – foundations, people with personal wealth are – that there are enough of them out there to support a flowering of this kind of thing? What’s your reading on that?

Yeah, I think that there’s enough money around. I think that there are enough people around with a large amount of cash and wealthy people that could provide this kind of support to institutions like the Artists Collective and other places that are trying to present cultural activities to the community and to the city. I think that it’s just very difficult to garner that money. It took, like I said, Dollie 15 years to raise that money for this building.
